newsitem.title: INDIA: Security costs mount for Miss World in India.
newsitem.headline: Security costs mount for Miss World in India.

text.p: Organisers of the Miss World beauty contest will have to foot a heavy security bill for bringing the beauty contest to India for the first time, a minister of the Karnataka state government said on Monday.

Protestors, ranging from womens groups to farmers and Hindu nationalists, have banded together in an anti-Miss World campaign to oppose the show being held in this southern Indian city later this month.

The Bangalore police plan to deploy more than 12,000 officers to safeguard the event, which is being touted by the Amitabh Bachchan Corp Ltd, which holds the licence to stage this year's contest, as a showcase for the "Garden City" of India.

"It involves a big security operation. We have asked them (the organisers) to pay the amount as it is a private show," Karnataka state home affairs minister Roshan Baig said after meeting with senior police and government officials.
Baig said he did not want to spell out the exact figure, although he has estimated the cost previously at over 22 million rupees ($562,000).
Baig also met with opposition groups to try to smooth the way for the pageant to be held in Bangalore later this month, but the opposition remained steadfast.

The vehemence of the protests against hosting the beauty contest in India has already persuaded the organisers to hold the swimsuit stage of the contest in Seychelles, in the Indian Ocean, later this week.

Baig also announced that the organisers had shifted two sub-events from the city to the outskirts because of the protests. But he said there was no question of shifting the main event to be held at Bangalore's Chinnaswamy Cricket Stadium on November 23.
"Para-military units of the border security force and the rapid action force will be on duty. We will see that nothing untoward happens at the show," Baig said.
